title: Test, pack, price and grow your cleaning products range
course_title: Detergent & Cleaning Products Production: A Six-Product Workshop

say: Test, pack, price and grow your cleaning products range.
This is the video for module 4: Quality Release, Packaging, Pricing and Scaling Up.
A product is ready to sell only when it passes tests you can repeat.
You need pH strips, a scale, a funnel, a phone timer and a few clear bottles.
For example, Funke checks her dish batch DL-07 before delivery.

panel.rule: No bottle below the label fill weight, even if the average is fine.

say: Packaging must resist the chemical inside and protect people.
HDPE suits acids, alkalis and disinfectants.
Acid and disinfectant products sold to homes should have child-resistant caps.
Give each product its own colour band, so a cleaner can tell toilet gel from dish liquid at a glance.

panel.heading: Containers that protect people
left: A different look for each product
right: A registration number before you have it

say: Never use drink bottles. Children have swallowed chemicals from familiar bottles. And print your NAFDAC number only once you have it, never before.

say: Every label carries the product name, the net content that matches your fill weight, and directions with the dose.

panel.heading: What every label carries
items: Directions with dose and contact time
Warnings, first aid, do not mix

say: It carries warnings and first aid, including do not mix with other products.

say: And a batch code. For example, Ifeoma in Asaba codes her second dish batch made on 5 October 2026 as DL-261005-02. The same code goes on the batch sheet, test card, retained sample and every bottle.

say: The batch costs 21,750 naira. Divided by 19 bottles, that is about 1,145 naira per bottle. Any price below that loses money.

say: Survey three competing products and convert each to price per litre, so you compare like with like.
Chiamaka sets a wholesale price of 1,700 naira. Her profit is 555 naira per bottle, or 10,550 naira per batch.
Her retail price is 2,000 naira, which earns 16,250 naira per batch.
A reseller who buys at 1,700 and sells at 2,000 earns 300 naira per bottle, so shops have a reason to stock her.
Screenshots and SMS alerts can be faked. Confirm the money in your own bank or wallet app before you deliver.

panel.heading: Wholesale and retail
panel.rule: Confirm money in your own account before releasing goods.

say: Growth usually comes from one or two institutions ordering every week.
Scale with a schedule, not just a bigger drum.
Make acid, alkaline and disinfectant products on different days, and wash drums between products.

cards.d: Acid, alkaline and disinfectant products on different days or drums. Test before filling.
Same order of addition, more caustic portions, longer waits. Never lift drums alone.
Five women each needing 8 kg LABSA buy 40 kg together and save 2,400 naira each a month.

say: At 100 kg, a splash means more chemical and more heat. Keep the same order of addition, add caustic in more portions, and train every member in PPE and first aid.

say: Many women grow faster together.
For example, five women in a Lagos market group each use 8 kg of LABSA a month.
Buying 40 kg together, with illustrative prices, they each save 2,400 naira a month.
They agree in writing who receives it and how it is weighed out.

say: To remember.
Run the five checks on every batch and keep a sample.
Pack in the right container, never a drink bottle.
Cost every batch, including your labour.
And as you grow, keep acids, alkalis and disinfectants apart.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Test card: appearance, pH, flow, fill, performance
Keep a retained sample from every batch
HDPE and child-resistant caps; no drink bottles
Separate chemistry by day as you scale
